## Introduction

This document demonstrates how to combine Markdown text with executable R code chunks in classic R Markdown (`.Rmd`), rendered with the `rmarkdown`/`knitr` packages. This is the format Quarto's `.qmd` files were built on top of - the chunk syntax is nearly identical, but the YAML header options are R Markdown's own (snake_case, under an `output:` key) rather than Quarto's.

## Selection Intensity by Selected Fraction

Selection intensity ($i$) measures how much better the selected group's mean is than the population mean, in standard deviation units, for a given selected fraction. Below, we compute and plot it across a range of selection intensities.

```{r fig-selection-intensity, fig.cap="Selection intensity as a function of the selected proportion", warning=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)

selected_fraction <- seq(0.01, 0.99, by = 0.01)
# Standard normal-distribution approximation of selection intensity:
# i = phi(z) / p, where z is the truncation point and phi is the standard
# normal density.
z <- qnorm(1 - selected_fraction)
intensity <- dnorm(z) / selected_fraction

df <- data.frame(selected_fraction = selected_fraction, intensity = intensity)

ggplot(df, aes(x = selected_fraction, y = intensity)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, color = "#2c7fb8") +
  labs(
    title = "Selection Intensity vs. Selected Fraction",
    x = "Fraction selected",
    y = "Selection intensity (i)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Takeaway

Selection intensity climbs quickly as the selected fraction shrinks below about 20%, but with rapidly diminishing returns - going from 10% to 1% selected buys much less extra intensity than going from 50% to 10% did.
